hints: Focus on what hot, concentrated acidified manganate(VII) does to alkenes, it completely breaks the C=C double bond.
Notice that each carbon of the C=C becomes its own product, so for only one carbon product both sides must give the same molecule.
Check each alkene for symmetry around the double bond and see which one splits into two identical fragments.
walkthrough:
**Recall the reaction type**

Hot, concentrated $\text{MnO}_4^- / \text{H}^+$ causes oxidative cleavage of alkenes. The C=C bond is broken completely and each C becomes a carbonyl compound.

Rule: $\text{RCH=CHR'} \rightarrow \text{RCOOH} + \text{R'COOH}$ (hot, conc. conditions)

**Apply the single product condition**

For only one carbon-containing product, the two fragments must be identical. That means the alkene must be symmetrical about the double bond.

Think: $\text{left side} = \text{right side}$ gives $1$ product, not $2$.

**Test the options**

$\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CHCH}_3$ is symmetrical but-2-ene. Both C atoms of C=C have a $\text{CH}_3$ group attached.

Cleavage: $$\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CHCH}_3 \rightarrow 2\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$$
Only ethanoic acid is formed as the carbon product, so this fits.

options.A: Incorrect. $\text{CH}_2\text{=C(CH}_3)_2$ is 2-methylpropene and is unsymmetrical. Cleavage gives propanone, $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C=O}$, from the right carbon and $\text{CO}_2$ from the $\text{=CH}_2$ left carbon, so two different carbon-containing products.
options.B: Correct. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CHCH}_3$ is but-2-ene, symmetrical about the C=C bond. Hot concentrated oxidation cleaves it to give two moles of the same acid, ethanoic acid $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$, so there is only a single carbon-containing product.
options.C: Incorrect. $\text{CH}_2\text{=CHCH}_2\text{CH}_3$ is but-1-ene and is unsymmetrical. Cleavage gives $\text{CO}_2$ from the $\text{=CH}_2$ end and propanoic acid $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$ from the other end, so two different carbon-containing products.
options.D: Incorrect. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ is butane, an alkane with no C=C bond. It is unreactive to acidified $\text{KMnO}_4$ under these conditions, so it gives no carbon-containing oxidation product at all.
